title: Dragon Worship
paragraphs: So, when I inspected the town to check the employees’ living quarters… it seemed even worse than the back alleys of Zeltoble. It was worse than a working-class neighborhood during wartime… It felt like people were doing just enough to survive. Takt did put a fair amount of effort into medical and welfare services—incorporating alchemy and other methods—so treatment for illnesses and deaths seemed to be affordable. However, it’s said they also imposed strict quotas and operated a system where medical supplies would be cut off if people didn’t work. In many ways, it’s said that their system—one designed to keep people barely alive while milking them for money—was exceptionally well-organized.

Incidentally, in Shieldfreeden, it seems a project was underway to pave the roads in each city with asphalt as part of road improvement efforts. Large trucks were even being manufactured, and it appears they planned to boost the flow of goods. The problem is securing fuel, though… I hear these vehicles run on some kind of technology that Takt and those swine kept secret? I’m not entirely sure, but we’re waiting for the analysis results.

In the first world… I believe I heard that a merchant from Zeltoble purchased the technology and built a Magic engine. Well, apparently it wasn’t very profitable because of the Filolials and their kind. Either way, I just can’t understand this policy of trying to thoroughly eradicate the Filolials.
After finishing our factory tour, we returned to the capital of Shieldfreeden via the portal. Father is holding his head in his hands, his fist pressed against his brow.

“I feel like I’ve seen the dark side of that whole ‘make a fortune with my invention’ story. Money is something that rots if you don’t put it to work, yet they hoarded it without ever doing anything with it… If only they’d at least shown some mercy by compensating the business rivals they’d defeated… Instead, they’re systematically crushing them…”
“It seems that culture is declining in various ways because of the rampages caused by reincarnated individuals.”

“They were probably creating inventions that wouldn’t stand the test of time and using them to wipe out existing products… It’d be nice if even good things could survive, but they won’t, so the enemy is playing their cards pretty well.”

It’s a strategy that’s far too long-term—exceeding the lifespan of a human. It means that once things proceed exactly as the enemy intends and reach the final stage, defeat is already a foregone conclusion. In that sense, they’re a truly devious enemy.
“As for me, I got to see a lot and had a decent time, though. I’ve honed my eye for spotting things that’ll turn a profit on the battlefield.”
“Lasa, you’re really resilient…”
“So? From the Shield Hero’s perspective, do you think we could manage Shieldfreeden as a vassal state?”

That’s right. Unlike before, we’ll now be under the jurisdiction of Siltvelt. The key question is whether we can use Shieldfreeden to our advantage against the Wave. That said, it looked like it was in shambles because of Takt.

“Honestly, forget about reparations—our finances are in dire straits due to debts and the like. I can’t even imagine a future where things would work out, even if we confiscated all the lawmakers’ profits and poured them into the budget.”
“Even so, do you realize it’s best to stop him from using the Shield Hero’s rights to halt the payment of reparations?”
“Hmm… Honestly, after seeing that devastation, I’m starting to waver—I’m beginning to think we might actually have to go that far.”

“Listen. I’ve been told the same thing by all four representatives of Siltvelt, so I don’t know the details either. But if we were to stop the claims for compensation, it wouldn’t set a good example for the other nations, and it could set a dangerous precedent.”

“…I suppose so. It really feels like we’re backed into a corner… Going out to capture the remaining Takt forces and recover the stolen money actually starts to look like the most constructive option.”
That means we’ve been cornered that much, doesn’t it? If even Father is throwing in the towel, those guys’ determination is truly terrifying.
“Should we turn the place into a wasteland? We could flush out the remnants, and if we sell the land to Zeltoble by the tsubo, we’d make some money, too.”

“Motoyasu, just keep quiet about this. There’s still… a chance we can pull through if the people unite, and—though I hate to say it—we’ll probably have to implement major reforms. Ah… I feel like a serious, hard-working politician right now.”
Are there actually any serious politicians out there? Maybe there’s a difference between my image of them and the reality in your world, Father.

“It seems Faubrey confiscated Takt’s assets, but even so, a considerable amount must have slipped through the cracks… Since that was Takt’s personal money, there are rumors that he must have other hidden assets as well.”
“I don’t think it’s wise to rely too much on hidden treasure. After all, that money doesn’t really belong to Shieldfreeden, does it?”
“That’s true… Nominally, it’s definitely going to Faubrey. This is going to be a mess. We’ll have to have an investigation to determine exactly what constitutes Shieldfreeden’s money…”

It seems Father wrapped up his testimony along those lines before heading into his meeting with the Shieldfreeden lawmakers. A heavy atmosphere hangs in the air. After all, the lawmakers are well aware that Father inspected Takt’s factory.
“I did, indeed, have the opportunity to tour Shieldfreeden’s production facility.”
Father explains to the lawmakers in somewhat grandiloquent language.

“There seems to be a stark contrast between what’s shown on the surface and what’s really going on behind the scenes. And they’re kept in a state of limbo—neither alive nor dead… It was a working environment that would make even a slave trader turn pale.”

A slave trader, you say? In a sense, I certainly felt as though I’d been forced to witness slavery. But… it’s true that the working conditions might actually be worse than those of slaves. In that situation, they’re essentially slaves forced into a harsh environment, lacking only the official slave mark.

By the way, in this world, the status of a slave—aside from torture slaves, duel slaves, and sex slaves—isn’t actually that bad. After all, they’re only forced to work. Slaves are fairly valuable assets, you see. If their bodies were ruined, it would be a total loss.
“I’m actually impressed that riots didn’t break out more often. Wait, come to think of it, the riots were suppressed and swept under the rug, weren’t they…? I really do feel sorry for them.”
“Y-yes…”

The members of the Takt faction do, after all, possess enough strength to break through their limits. If they’d tried to riot recklessly, they would’ve been suppressed by force. On top of that, the bureaucrats were completely corrupt and deeply entrenched… It must have been a hopeless situation.

What kind of hellish country is this? With a territory this large and politics like this, the future looks bleak. After all, it’s a country that was created by combining Zeltoble and Faubrey and then deteriorating in every way.

“First, our policy must be to improve our nation’s production capacity while capturing the remnants of Takt and recovering the vast sums of money that were stolen—and then we’ll need to further boost our production capacity. To do that, we’ll have to raise taxes on the people; otherwise, it’ll be impossible to pay the massive reparations.”
“B-but! If you do something like that, riots will definitely break out!　Do you Heroes intend to exploit Shieldfreeden just like Nelshen and Takt did!?”
“You’re being quite defiant. Well then, shall we just wipe this country off the map and pretend it never existed? That way, we won’t have to worry about money at all.”
“……It’s not like I’m doing this because I want to, you know. I’m only saying this because I can still see some areas where the people of Shieldfreeden have a little leeway in their lives.”
I hear that a stark disparity between the wealthy and the lower classes is a defining feature of Shieldfreeden. Father must have seen a way forward in narrowing that gap.

“Since the people in the factory district have essentially already paid, let’s leave them as is… As for the remaining wealthy individuals, we’ll just have to compensate them for that amount. We should be able to buy some time before paying the compensation. Under the current circumstances, fleeing the country would likely be treated as an act of allegiance to the Takt faction.”

At Father’s remark, the lawmakers clenched their fists, looking as if they wanted to object. But that’s impossible, you see. I won’t allow it. Still… there really aren’t any decent people among lawmakers and nobles, are there?
“I understand the Hero’s opinion. However, there is one… very significant problem that has come to light in our national survey here in Shieldfreeden.”
“…What is it now?”
“First, regarding the wealthy and middle classes, the overwhelming majority have stated that, for certain reasons, they cannot submit to the authority of the Shield Hero.”
When Father turned his gaze toward the envoys from Siltvelt, they nodded in agreement. Are they still saying things like that?
“The lower classes, like those in Siltvelt, do revere the Shield Hero…”
“If the lower classes, the wealthy, and the middle class all belong to the same denomination, why is this happening? What is the reason?”
Father asked, tilting his head as if the matter were a bother.

“Well… that’s… largely due to the existence of the Aotatsu race and the Divine Dragons, which are central to our faith here in Shieldfreeden. It was precisely because Takt was favored by both of them that he was able to outshine the Hammer Hero and enjoyed such strong support and trust from the people…”

Come to think of it, given the events leading up to this point, the Hero wielding the Hammer’s Seven-Star Weapon had been completely forgotten. It’s such a humiliating situation that no one even seemed to be aware of him.

According to the story, there was a time when Shieldfreeden somehow managed to wrest the rights to the Seven-Star Hammer from Siltvelt. And yet, look how he’s being treated. Even though he’s already been erased by Takt, it’s truly pitiful.

But don’t worry. In the first world, he was recognized as the bearer by my Older Sister! He even rose to become the weapon that serves as Father’s right-hand man—the most important role of all… He’s the rising star of the Seven-Star Weapons! Though I don’t know about this particular instance.
“In other words, it’s not just a matter of them being opposed to him.”
Come to think of it, the workers reacted favorably toward Father. Was that also because they were from the lower classes, where the Shield Faith runs deep?
“What about the Divine Dragon?”

“Yes… According to the story, the heroes defeated a dragon said to be the reincarnation of the Divine Dragon worshipped in Shieldfreeden. Even if a new Blue Dragon representative were dispatched from Siltvelt, I doubt they’d be able to recruit from the upper and middle classes unless this issue is resolved.”
This is the kind of hassle that arises precisely because it’s a so-called democracy. That said, if the reason is clear, there probably is a solution. But a Divine Dragon… a dragon, you say…?

“So, while the official religion venerates the Shield Hero, in reality there are two sects within the country: the upper and middle classes practice dragon worship, while the lower classes have a deep-rooted faith in the Shield Hero?”

The fact that the factory workers went out of their way to leave behind actual bottles of “Corporate Slave Drink” might be a sign that they don’t trust the upper echelons of Shieldfreeden—in other words, the wealthy. A vast gap in perception, rooted in religion, has formed between the wealthy and the lower classes.
Is this the major difference between Shieldfreeden and Siltvelt? They really are a troublesome lot. Just as I was thinking this, the people from Siltvelt spoke up.
“Does Shieldfreeden even understand that it’s a defeated nation?”
“You lot are the invaders!”

“It’s only by the mercy of the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero that things have turned out this way! This is a country that conspired with Takt, the enemy of the world. It wouldn’t be out of place to confiscate all their property and enslave every single citizen!”

The people of Siltvelt seem to be quite outraged. Even I think that would be going too far, but I can understand how they feel. If it’s okay to just get fed up with the whole thing and hand it all over in the end, then isn’t that fine?
“Do you even understand your own position?!”

“However, it’s also a fact that the citizens are currently obstructing the investigation into Takt’s faction. I think it’ll be difficult unless we do something about this issue. I say this fully prepared to face the consequences!”
One of the Shieldfreeden councilors spoke forcefully to Father.

Well, then, why not just punish them? We should make them understand where they stand. After all, Faubrey himself has issued a proclamation declaring that anyone harboring members of the Takt faction is an enemy of the world, so that should provide a legitimate justification for confiscating their assets. If they think it’s fine as long as they don’t get caught, then they’re beyond redemption.
Just as the people of Siltvelt were about to rise again in response to such rude behavior, Father raised one hand to stop them.

“So… you’re saying that in Shieldfreeden’s religious circles, as long as the Shield Hero doesn’t win over the Aotatsu species—or some other powerful dragon that’s beloved by the people—as an object of worship other than himself, the wealthy and middle classes won’t part with a single coin, even if it kills them… is that right?”
“Yes. Therefore, I humbly propose that you, the Heroes, command a powerful dragon to serve as the nation’s new symbol.”
“Well, if it’s just that much…”
Father was about to make a concession. Right then, a voice echoed in my head.
“Yayyy. It’s my turn!”
I’m pretty sure that’s how it went. You’re not invited here! Brionac!
“I’m making my debut in seven more episodes!”
It’s not April Fools’ Day today! I turned Rival into a beam of Light in my head. Father, don’t let yourself be swayed.
“Tame a dragon…? That’s out of the question.”

All dragons are enemies. Whether they turn into Dragon Kings, try to curry favor, piggyback on the loop, turn into chocolate, or refuse to speak even though they can—they’re nothing but a nuisance. Especially that noisy guy who hitches a ride on the loop to cozy up to Father—he’s completely out of the question. Just like in the last world, they should just keep quiet.
“Come out one by one! No, I’m going to kill you all right now!”
I’ll climb onto the table and brandish my spear! Of all things, telling Father to raise a dragon—what on earth were they thinking?! I absolutely will not forgive this!
“Motoyasu, calm down!”
Father is scolding me, but this is a matter I simply cannot compromise on. So what if there’s a dragon?
I’ll wipe out anyone who practices that kind of faith! And harboring the Takt faction—unless Father makes arrangements—is utterly outrageous! It’s a crime worthy of death.
In fact, we don’t even need a dragon. That was proven in the last loop! Even without any Limit Breaks, as long as Father and I are here, we can figure this out together!
“I understand how you feel, but please try to hold it in for now!”
Father stood up and put me in a bear hug. Ugh! If it weren’t for Father, I’d have shaken him off by now! When I relaxed my grip, Father said,

“…I highly commend you for speaking your mind so strongly to us, even in a situation like this, out of concern for the country. I understand… but I’d like you to wait just a little while. The meeting has reached an impasse, so let’s take a short break.”
“Yes. I’m the one who’s sorry. I realize that someone like me shouldn’t really be offering opinions in the first place. But please… I pray that you, the Heroes, will accept this proposal.”
With that, we ended up taking a break in a separate room. Father took me by the hand and led me to the break room.
Note: This is entirely a figment of Yari’s imagination and does not represent the actual person.
